<context>
You are an expert at solving ARC-AGI (Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus) puzzles using Answer Set Programming (ASP).

ARC-AGI puzzles show input-output grid transformations. Each cell contains a color value (integer 0–9). The goal is to discover the hidden transformation rule from training examples and encode it as an ASP program.
</context>

<rules>
- `input(row, col, color)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- `color(0..9)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- the output predicate is always `output(row, col, color)` — do not redefine it.
- the final program must produce exactly one answer set, in which `output(row, col, color)` match the expected output exactly.
- end your program with `#show output/3.`
</rules>

<example_1>
This puzzle copies the input to the output unchanged.

<grid_1>
Input:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>

Output:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>
</grid_1>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Copy each input cell to the output unchanged
output(R, C, Color) :- input(R, C, Color).

#show output/3.
</asp>
</example_1>

<example_2>
This puzzle replaces every non-zero cell with color 5; zero cells stay 0.

<grid_1>
Input:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>

Output:
<diagram>

5 0 5
0 5 0
</diagram>
</grid_1>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Recolor every non-zero cell to 5; zeros stay 0.
output(R, C, 5) :- input(R, C, V), V != 0.
output(R, C, 0) :- input(R, C, 0).

#show output/3.
</asp>
</example_2>

<example_3>

<grid_1>

</diagram>

</diagram>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Mirror: column C of the output is column (M-1-C) of the input.
output(R, C, Color) :- input(R, Cin, Color), n_cols(M), C = M - 1 - Cin.

#show output/3.
</asp>
</example_3>

% Dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R,_,_) }.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{C : input(_,C,_)}.
row(0..N-1).
col(0..M-1).

% Cells with at least one orthogonal non‑zero neighbour
has_neighbor(R,C,Color) :-
    input(R,C,Color), Color != 0,
    ( (R+1 < N, input(R+1,_,_,Col), Col != 0) ;
      (R-1 >= 0, input(R-1,_,_,Col), Col != 0) ;
      (C+1 < M, input(R,_,_,Col), Col != 0) ;
      (C-1 >= 0, input(R,_,_,Col), Col != 0) ).

shape(R,C,Color) :- has_neighbor(R,C,Color).

% Number of orthogonal shape neighbours
neighbor_count(R,C,Count) :-
    shape(R,C,Color), Count = #count{
        (R2,C2,_Color2) : shape(R2,C2,Color2),
              R2 = R+1, C2 = C ;
              R2 = R-1, C2 = C ;
              R2 = R,   C2 = C+1 ;
              R2 = R,   C2 = C-1 }.

% Choose the centre cell:
%  – maximal neighbour count,
%  – among those with equal count, choose the smallest column.
center(Rc,Cc,Colorc) :-
    shape(Rc,Cc,Colorc), neighbor_count(Rc,Cc,Nc),
    not shape(R2,C2,Color2), neighbor_count(R2,C2,Nc2), Nc < Nc2.
center(Rc,Cc,Colorc) :-
    shape(Rc,Cc,Colorc), neighbor_count(Rc,Cc,Nc),
    not shape(R2,Cc2,Color2), neighbor_count(R2,Cc2,Nc2), Nc = Nc2, Cc < Cc2.

% Isolated colour‑5 (there is at most one)
solo5_r, solo5_c :- input(solo5_r,solo5_c,5), not shape(solo5_r,solo5_c,5).

% Centre coordinates
center_r(Rc) :- center(Rc,Cc,Colorc).
center_c(Cc) :- center(Rc,Cc,Colorc).

% Translation offsets
dr = 0, dc = 0 :- not solo5_r.          % no solitary 5 → no translation
dr = solo5_r - centre_r, dc = solo5_c - centre_c :- solo5_r.

% Copy the shape using the translation (keep colour)
shape_copy(R2,C2,Color) :-
    shape(R,C,Color),
    R2 = R + dr,
    C2 = C + dc,
    R2 >= 0, R2 < N,
    C2 >= 0, C2 < M.

% Build the output
output(R,C,Color) :- shape_copy(R,C,Color).
output(R,C,0)   :- not shape_copy(R,C).

#show output/3.

col(0..M-1) :- col(0..M-1).

    ( (R+1 < N, input(R+1,_,_,C2), C2 != 0) ;
      (R-1 >= 0, input(R-1,_,_,C2), C2 != 0) ;
      (C+1 < M, input(R,_,_,C3), C3 != 0) ;
      (C-1 >= 0, input(R,_,_,C4), C4 != 0) ).

% Dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R,_,_) }.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{C : input(_,C,_)}.
row(0..N-1).
col(0..M-1).

% Helper: has at least one orthogonal non-zero neighbour
has_neighbor(R,C,Color) :-
    input(R,C,Color), Color != 0,
    ( (R+1 < N, input(R+1,_,_,Col), Col != 0) ;
      (R-1 >= 0, input(R-1,_,_,Col), Col != 0) ;
      (C+1 < M, input(R,_,_,Col), Col != 0) ;
      (C-1 >= 0, input(R,_,_,Col), Col != 0) ).

shape(R,C,Color) :- has_neighbor(R,C,Color).

% Neighbor count
neighbor_count(R,C,Count) :-
    shape(R,C,Color), Count = #count{
        (R2,C2,_Color2) : shape(R2,C2,Color2),
              R2 = R+1, C2 = C ;
              R2 = R-1, C2 = C ;
              R2 = R,   C2 = C+1 ;
              R2 = R,   C2 = C-1 }.

% Choose centre cell: maximal neighbour count, tie‑break by lowest column (i.e. smallest column)
center(Rc,Cc,Colorc) :-
    shape(Rc,Cc,Colorc), neighbor_count(Rc,Cc,Nc),

% Build output

output(R,C,0)   :- not shape_copy(R,C).
